chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who gave his mother a gift. So she died, and she had taken possession of that which he had given her and was irrevocably freed from it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He and the inheritors are equal with regards to it'.
ai.seo_question: Does a mother's gift to her son revert to him if she dies before returning it?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that a gift (*hibah*) given by a son to his mother becomes irrevocable upon her acceptance and possession, meaning it fully enters her estate upon death. This ruling distinguishes the gift from a loan or conditional transfer, ensuring it is distributed among all heirs equally rather than reverting solely to the giver. This highlights the Shia legal principle of *qabd* (possession) as the key determinant for the finality of gifts in inheritance matters.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who gave his mother a gift. So she died and she had taken possession of that which he had given her and was irrevocably freed from it. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Him and the other inheritors are equal with regards to it’.
en.sarwar: 16. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu as from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah who has narrated the following: “I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who gives a gift to his mother and she dies. She had taken the gift away from him in her possession.
He (the Imam) said, ‘He and the other heirs are the same in dealing with that item.’”
